correctness.rationale: Exact algebra from the original two-dimensional recurrence gives I↦S(I), r(I); S increases strictly and c≥w ensures r(I) strictly increasing from r_c to infinity. The endemic-versus-disease-free difference reduces to h(I)/b. The explicit derivative L′=(c-w)aβ exp(-βI)/[(1+cz)(1+wz)] strictly decreases when c>w; strict convexity of h and bounded L imply the full trichotomy and uniqueness of the positive crossing, with w=1 degenerate cases treated separately. For d=1/4, w=μ=0, b=β=1 the exact cross equation factors (1-t)(1-3t), and the Jacobian satisfies three explicitly positive Schur conditions using 1<ln3<2. The bundled checker recomputes identities and 25 sample residuals but is not the proof.

value.rationale: The source poses infection-induced population size increase at endemic steady states as a biological mathematical phenomenon and supplies only conservative sufficient conditions. A complete and sharp reproduction-rate regime partition—whether gain is always present, turns on once, or is absent—resolves the precise motivated comparison and excludes repeated reversals in a nonlinear overcompensatory map. The worked local-sink crossover provides a meaningful dynamically stable instance missed by the published sufficient wedge; the result is not an arbitrary numeric slice.
